title: Longest Consecutive Run
hints: Put everything in a `Set` for O(1) lookups.
Only start counting a run at its **first** number — where `n - 1` isn't in the set — then count upwards.
`for n in set where !set.contains(n - 1) { var len = 1; while set.contains(n + len) { len += 1 }; best = max(best, len) }`.
jsBridge: The same O(n) set-based algorithm as in JS. Swift's `Set.contains` is an O(1) hash lookup, and the "only start at run beginnings" trick is what keeps it linear.

compass.q: Sorting first (O(n log n)) vs the set trick (O(n)): at what n does the difference show up on-device?
Why does `for x in set where !set.contains(x - 1)` keep it O(n) even though there's a nested while loop?
In JS, `Set` of numbers is keyed by SameValueZero. Is Swift's `Set<Int>` any different for negatives and zero?
Streaks ("7 days in a row") are this problem with dates. Why is `Calendar` arithmetic needed instead of plain integers?
